note:
Six model-application images for the homepage review slider, one per product. Tatcha's own review images were downloaded and examined rather than described from memory: square, tight crop on the face, a VISIBLE SWATCH OF PRODUCT ON THE CHEEK, a hand at the face, a pale neutral grey-beige seamless backdrop, soft even light, minimal makeup. The swatch is the detail that makes them read as 'in use' rather than as portraits, so every brief below names it.

Deliberately light, not graphite. The review section sits on #f7f7f7 and the hero carries the dark register; a dark review strip would fight both. This matches Tatcha and matches the review image already live.

Casting follows the standard Malcolm set — Caucasian, around thirty-five — but age, hair and colouring are varied across the six so they read as six different customers rather than one model six times. Flagged for him: Tatcha's set is deliberately diverse across ethnicity, and six reviews from one demographic reads narrower than a real customer base.

Class B throughout: no bottle in frame, only the substance on skin, so there is no branding for a generator to invent. Substance colours follow the agreed product-colour table, not invention.

v2 after Malcolm's review: casting varied across ethnicities to match Tatcha's set (he confirmed different people types are wanted), and the crop tightened hard — v1 framed whole heads with air around them where Tatcha's cut the top of the head off and fill the frame with cheek and eye. The Glutathione swatch is also re-specified as a transparent wet film, since v1 rendered it as an opaque flaky white.

v3 after Malcolm: models should be beautiful, and should be APPLYING the product rather than holding a decorative pose. v2's hands rested against the face beside a static swatch, which read as a portrait with product added. Every brief now names a specific application gesture caught mid motion — smoothing, patting, drawing upward, pressing, circling, tapping — with un-blended product visible ahead of the fingers and a smoothed film behind, and 'hand resting idly' is negated.

slots.title: Review image 1 — Copper Peptide Renewal Serum
slots.prompt: Editorial beauty photograph, square format, an extremely tight close up of the face of a strikingly beautiful Black woman around thirty two years old with high cheekbones and close cropped dark hair. The crop is very close: her face fills the entire frame edge to edge, the top of her head is cut off by the upper edge and her chin sits near the lower edge, so only cheek, eye, nose and mouth are in frame. She is turned three quarters toward the camera, her expression calm and self possessed. She is actively applying blue serum, colour #2F6FD0 to her face right now. Two fingertips press flat against her cheekbone and are smoothing the serum outward along the bone, caught mid stroke, the product visibly spreading into a glossy film under her fingers with a little still un-blended ahead of them. This is a genuine application gesture, mid action, not a hand resting decoratively against the face. Beautiful, well groomed, flawless even complexion, but with real skin kept real: visible pores and natural texture, no plastic smoothing. Minimal makeup, bare lips, short unpainted nails. Behind her a seamless pale neutral grey backdrop, colour #D8D6D4, evenly lit and almost entirely hidden by the closeness of the crop. Soft broad key light from the front with a gentle fill, no hard shadows. 100mm lens at f4, natural skin tones, clean neutral grade.
